questions.question: Which of the following states had benefitted by the Indira Gandhi Canal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indira Gandhi Canal, previously known as the Rajasthan Canal, is one of the largest canal projects in India.
 
• It primarily benefits the state of Rajasthan, especially the north-western part of the state.
 
• The canal provides irrigation facilities to the arid and semi-arid regions of Rajasthan, transforming the desert areas into fertile lands.
 
• The project has significantly contributed to the agricultural development and economic upliftment of the region.
 
• The canal also supplies drinking water to several districts in Rajasthan, enhancing the quality of life for the local population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indira Gandhi Canal Project**

 
 
• It is the longest canal in India, with a total length of approximately 650 kilometers.
 
• The project was initiated in 1958 and completed in the 1980s, named after the former Prime Minister of India, Indira Gandhi.
 
• The main source of water for the canal is the Sutlej and Beas rivers, and it is a part of the larger Bhakra-Nangal Project.
 
• The canal traverses through the Thar Desert, one of the most arid regions in India.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Agriculture**
 
 
• The canal has facilitated the cultivation of crops like wheat, mustard, cotton, and groundnut in regions that were previously desert.
 
• It has led to the introduction of modern irrigation techniques and increased the use of fertilizers and improved seeds, boosting agricultural productivity.
 
 
 
• **Drinking Water Supply**
 
 
• Besides irrigation, the canal also plays a crucial role in providing drinking water to cities like Bikaner, Jaisalmer, and Barmer.
 
• This has helped in alleviating water scarcity issues in these regions, especially during summer months.
 
 
 
• **Environmental and Social Impact**
 
 
• The project has led to the creation of green belts and afforestation in the canal's command area.
 
• It has also led to socio-economic changes by providing employment opportunities and improving living standards in rural Rajasthan.

questions.question: Which of the following is the style of temple architecture that is widely favoured in northern India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Nagar** is the style of temple architecture that is predominantly found in northern India.
 
• This architectural style is characterized by its **curvilinear towers** known as Shikhara.
 
• Nagar temples typically have a square sanctum (Garbha Griha) with a central tower.
 
• Examples of Nagar architecture include the **Kandariya Mahadeva Temple** in Khajuraho and the **Sun Temple** in Modhera.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vihar**

 
 
• Vihar refers to Buddhist monastic dwellings, not to temple architecture.
 
• These structures were used as residences for monks and places for meditation and learning.
 
 
 
• **Mandapa**
 
 
• Mandapa is a pillared hall or pavilion in Indian architecture, often used as an entrance to a temple.
 
• It is not a style of temple architecture but an integral part of temple design.
 
 
 
• **Dravid**
 
 
• Dravid or Dravidian architecture is the style of temple architecture that is predominantly found in southern India.
 
• It is characterized by pyramid-shaped towers and intricate carvings.
 
• Examples include the Meenakshi Temple in Madurai and the Brihadeeswarar Temple in Thanjavur.
 
 
 
• **Temple Architecture in India**
 
 
• Indian temple architecture is classified into three main styles: Nagara (North Indian), Dravidian (South Indian), and Vesara (a mix of both).
 
• Each style has its distinct features and cultural significance.

questions.question: 'My Country My Life' is the autobiography of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lal Krishna Advani**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Lal Krishna Advani**, often referred to as L.K. Advani, is a prominent Indian politician and one of the founding members of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
 
• He served as the Deputy Prime Minister of India from 2002 to 2004 under Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.
 
• *My Country My Life* is his autobiography, published in 2008, detailing his political journey and experiences over several decades.
 
• The book provides an insight into the political landscape of India, especially focusing on the rise of the BJP and its major political strategies and campaigns.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)**

 
 
• The BJP is one of the two major political parties in India, the other being the Indian National Congress.
 
• Founded in 1980, the BJP follows the ideology of Hindutva and advocates for Hindu nationalism.
 
• The party has been in power at the central government multiple times, with significant leaders including Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Narendra Modi.
 
 
 
• **Atal Bihari Vajpayee**
 
 
• Atal Bihari Vajpayee was the 10th Prime Minister of India, serving three terms between 1996 and 2004.
 
• He was a senior leader of the BJP and played a crucial role in its growth and political strategies.
 
• Vajpayee is known for his efforts in economic reforms, nuclear tests, and improving India’s international relations.
 
 
 
• **Indian Political Landscape**
 
 
• India follows a multi-party system, with numerous regional and national parties.
 
• The political landscape has been dominated by the Congress Party for several decades post-independence, with the BJP emerging as a significant force in the late 20th century.
 
• Coalition politics has become common in India, often requiring parties to form alliances to achieve a majority in the parliament.
 
 
 
• **Autobiographies of Indian Politicians**
 
 
• Autobiographies offer a personal glimpse into the lives and careers of politicians, providing context to their decisions and ideologies.
 
• Other notable political autobiographies include "The Accidental Prime Minister" by Sanjaya Baru and "My Experiments with Truth" by Mahatma Gandhi.

questions.concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
questions.question: In which of the following systems was the charge of collecting the revenue and paying it to the Company given to the village headman, rather than the zamindar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahalwari**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Mahalwari system was a land revenue system implemented in British India.
 
• Under this system, the village headman, known as the 'lambardar,' was responsible for collecting revenue from the villagers.
 
• The revenue collected by the lambardar was then paid to the British East India Company.
 
• This system was introduced by Holt Mackenzie in 1822 and later modified by Lord William Bentinck in 1833.
 
• The Mahalwari system was primarily implemented in the North-Western Provinces, parts of Central India, and Punjab.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zamindari System**

 
 
• Also known as the Permanent Settlement System, it was introduced by Lord Cornwallis in 1793.
 
• Under this system, zamindars were recognized as the landowners and were responsible for collecting and paying revenue to the Company.
 
• The zamindars were granted hereditary rights over the land and were supposed to pay a fixed amount of revenue annually.
 
• This system was primarily implemented in Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa.
 
 
 
• **Ryotwari System**
 
 
• This system was introduced by Thomas Munro in 1820.
 
• Under the Ryotwari system, the individual cultivator or ryot was recognized as the landowner.
 
• The ryots were directly responsible for paying the land revenue to the British government.
 
• This system was primarily implemented in Madras, Bombay, parts of Assam, and Coorg provinces.
 
 
 
• **Iqtadari System**
 
 
• The Iqtadari system was introduced during the Delhi Sultanate period.
 
• Under this system, the land was divided into Iqtas, and the responsibility of collecting revenue was given to the Iqtadars.
 
• The Iqtadars were responsible for maintaining law and order and providing military assistance to the Sultan.

questions.question: Who among the following signed a pact with Lord Irwin on March 5, 1931?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on **March 5, 1931**.
 
• The agreement was between **Mahatma Gandhi** and the then Viceroy of India, Lord Irwin.
 
• As part of the pact, the Indian National Congress agreed to **participate in the Round Table Conference** in London.
 
• In return, the British government agreed to **release political prisoners** who were not involved in violence and to allow peaceful picketing of liquor and foreign cloth shops.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Salt March (Dandi March)**

 
 
• A non-violent protest against the British salt monopoly in colonial India led by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• The 24-day march began on March 12, 1930, and ended on April 6, 1930.
 
• It was a direct action campaign of tax resistance and nonviolent protest.
 
• The march is considered a pivotal event in the Indian independence movement.
 
 
 
• **Round Table Conferences**
 
 
• A series of three conferences organized by the British government to discuss constitutional reforms in India.
 
• The first conference was held in London from November 1930 to January 1931, the second from September to December 1931, and the third from November to December 1932.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi attended the second conference as the sole representative of the Indian National Congress.
 
 
 
• **Irwin Declaration**
 
 
• Also known as the "Delhi Declaration," it was issued by Lord Irwin on October 31, 1929.
 
• It promised a dominion status for India in an unspecified future.
 
• The declaration was a response to growing demands for self-governance in India.
 
 
 
• **Simon Commission**
 
 
• A group of seven British Members of Parliament sent to India in 1927 to study constitutional reform.
 
• The commission was met with widespread protests across India because it did not include any Indian members.
 
• The slogan "Simon Go Back" became popular during the protests.

questions.question: A river is capable of forming which of the following landscapes when the river is in its middle course?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A meander**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A meander is a bend or curve in a river, typically occurring in the river's middle course.
 
• In the middle course, the river has more energy and volume, promoting lateral (sideways) erosion rather than vertical erosion.
 
• Meanders form due to the erosion of the river banks on the outer side of bends and deposition on the inner side.
 
• This process is driven by the helicoidal flow of the river, which causes the water to corkscrew down its channel, enhancing the erosion and deposition cycles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Waterfalls:**

 
 
• Formed where rivers flow over hard rock followed by soft rock, leading to vertical erosion.
 
• Typically found in the upper course of the river.
 
 
 
• **Delta:**
 
 
• Formed at the river mouth where it meets a standing body of water like a sea or lake.
 
• Occurs due to deposition of sediment carried by the river as it loses energy upon entering the standing water.
 
 
 
• **V-shaped valley:**
 
 
• Characteristic of the upper course of a river.
 
• Formed by vertical erosion of the river cutting down into the bedrock.
 
 
 
• **Floodplains:**
 
 
• Flat areas adjacent to the river, formed by the deposition of sediment during floods.
 
• Common in the middle and lower courses of the river.

questions.question: Which of the following mountain peaks is a part of the Himalayas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kamet**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kamet** is the second highest mountain in the Garhwal region of Uttarakhand, India.
 
• It is a part of the **Himalayas** and specifically located in the Zanskar Range.
 
• Kamet stands at an elevation of **7,756 meters (25,446 feet)**.
 
• It is the third highest peak in India, outside of the Karakoram range.
 
• The peak was first summited in 1931 by Frank Smythe, Eric Shipton, and R.L. Holdsworth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Himalayas**

 
 
• The Himalayas are a mountain range in Asia, separating the plains of the Indian subcontinent from the Tibetan Plateau.
 
• The range has some of the planet's highest peaks, including the very highest, Mount Everest in Nepal.
 
• The Himalayas span five countries: Bhutan, India, Nepal, China, and Pakistan.
 
• The name "Himalaya" means "abode of snow" in Sanskrit, reflecting the vast amounts of snow and ice that cover the range.
 
 
 
• **Zanskar Range**
 
 
• The Zanskar Range is a mountain range in the union territory of Ladakh that separates Zanskar from Ladakh.
 
• It is a sub-range of the Himalayas and stretches from the eastern part of Ladakh to the Himachal Pradesh border.
 
• The range has many high peaks, with Kamet being one of the most prominent.
 
 
 
• **Mountaineering in India**
 
 
• India offers a variety of mountaineering opportunities, with the Himalayas being a prime destination.
 
• The Indian Mountaineering Foundation (IMF) is the apex body for mountaineering and allied sports in India.
 
• Several high-altitude peaks in India are popular among climbers, including Nanda Devi, Kanchenjunga, and Kamet.
 
 
 
• **Climatic Conditions**
 
 
• The Himalayas play a crucial role in influencing the climate of the Indian subcontinent, particularly the monsoon.
 
• The high peaks block cold winds from Central Asia, keeping South Asia warmer in winter.
 
• The range also causes orographic precipitation, leading to diverse ecosystems and weather patterns across the region.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT related to goals of Fundamental Duties of Indian Citizens?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Courage**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Fundamental Duties are enshrined in Part IVA of the Indian Constitution under Article 51A.
 
• They were added by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976, upon the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• These duties emphasize the responsibilities of Indian citizens to contribute to the nation’s unity, integrity, and sovereignty.
 
• Key goals include preserving the rich heritage, promoting harmony, protecting the environment, and respecting the Constitution and national institutions.
 
• Unlike the options "Preserve," "Cherish," and "Respect," the term "Courage" is not explicitly mentioned as a Fundamental Duty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties:**

 
 
• There are 11 Fundamental Duties listed in Article 51A of the Indian Constitution.
 
• They are moral obligations intended to promote a sense of discipline and commitment among citizens.
 
• These duties are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by courts for their violation.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Fundamental Duties:**
 
 
• To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag, and the National Anthem.
 
• To cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom.
 
• To protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife.
 
• To develop the scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act:**
 
 
• Also known as the "Mini-Constitution" due to its wide-ranging impact.
 
• It brought about significant changes to the Constitution, including the addition of Fundamental Duties.
 
• It aimed to strengthen the power of the central government and ensure the unity and integrity of the nation.
 
 
 
• **Swaran Singh Committee:**
 
 
• Formed in 1976 to make recommendations on the amendment of the Constitution.
 
• Suggested the inclusion of Fundamental Duties in the Constitution.
 
• Its recommendations led to the 42nd Amendment Act which added Part IVA to the Constitution.

questions.question: Which team won the Women's Asian Hockey Champions Trophy in 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India won the Women's Asian Hockey Champions Trophy in 2023.
 
• The tournament took place in Ranchi, Jharkhand, India.
 
• India defeated Japan in the final to secure the title.
 
• This victory marked India's fourth title in the history of the Women's Asian Hockey Champions Trophy.
 
• The Indian team displayed outstanding performance throughout the tournament, led by their captain Savita Punia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Women's Asian Hockey Champions Trophy**

 
 
• The Women's Asian Hockey Champions Trophy is an annual women's field hockey tournament for Asian teams, organized by the Asian Hockey Federation.
 
• The tournament features the top national teams from Asia competing for the title.
 
• It was first held in 2010 and has been a significant event in the women's field hockey calendar.
 
• The competition aims to promote and enhance the level of women's hockey in the Asian region.
 
 
 
• **Indian Women's Hockey Team**
 
 
• The Indian Women's Hockey Team has shown remarkable progress and consistency in recent years.
 
• The team is known for its strong defense, skillful midfield, and potent attack.
 
• Coached by Janneke Schopman, the team has achieved significant milestones on the international stage.
 
• Key players include Rani Rampal, Savita Punia, and Vandana Katariya.
 
 
 
• **Hockey in India**
 
 
• Hockey is a popular sport in India, with a rich history and tradition.
 
• India has won multiple Olympic medals in hockey, with the men's team being particularly successful historically.
 
• Efforts are being made to promote and develop women's hockey in the country.
 
• The Hockey India Federation governs the sport and organizes domestic and international competitions.

questions.question: S Abdul Nazeer was appointed as the Governor of ______ in February 2023.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Andhra Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• S Abdul Nazeer was appointed as the Governor of **Andhra Pradesh** on February 2023.
 
• His appointment came following the retirement of the previous Governor, Biswa Bhusan Harichandan, who was transferred to Chhattisgarh.
 
• Before his appointment as Governor, S Abdul Nazeer served as a judge in the Supreme Court of India.
 
• He has been involved in several landmark judgments, including the controversial Ayodhya case and the Triple Talaq case.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Role of a Governor in India**

 
 
• The Governor is the constitutional head of each state in India.
 
• Their duties are similar to those of the President of India but at the state level.
 
• They act on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister.
 
• Governors have the power to grant pardons, reprieves, and respites.
 
 
 
• **Supreme Court of India**
 
 
• It is the highest judicial forum and final court of appeal in India.
 
• It was established on January 28, 1950, two days after India became a republic.
 
• The Supreme Court consists of the Chief Justice of India and a sanctioned strength of 34 judges.
 
 
 
• **Ayodhya Verdict**
 
 
• Delivered on November 9, 2019, it resolved the long-standing dispute over the land in Ayodhya.
 
• The Supreme Court ruled in favor of building a Ram temple at the disputed site.
 
• The court also ordered the allocation of alternative land for the construction of a mosque.
 
 
 
• **Triple Talaq Case**
 
 
• A landmark judgment delivered on August 22, 2017.
 
• The Supreme Court declared the practice of instant triple talaq (talaq-e-biddat) as unconstitutional.
 
• The judgment led to the enactment of the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019.

questions.question: Which Tamil superstar founded the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) political party in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry on 2 February 2024 with the slogan 'Pirappokkum Ellaa Uyirkkum' (All are equal by birth)?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: The digestive enzymes inside lysosomes are made by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**rough endoplasmic reticulum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) is responsible for synthesizing digestive enzymes that are later transported to lysosomes.
 
• RER is characterized by the presence of ribosomes on its surface, which play a critical role in protein synthesis.
 
• Proteins synthesized in the RER are transported to the Golgi apparatus for further modification and sorting.
 
• Lysosomal enzymes are tagged with a specific marker, mannose-6-phosphate, in the Golgi apparatus before being directed to lysosomes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)**

 
 
• The ER is a network of membranous tubules and sacs that plays a key role in protein and lipid synthesis.
 
• There are two types of ER: rough ER, which is studded with ribosomes, and smooth ER, which lacks ribosomes.
 
• The smooth ER is involved in lipid synthesis and detoxification processes.
 
 
 
• **Golgi Apparatus**
 
 
• The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts, and packages proteins and lipids for secretion or delivery to other organelles.
 
• It consists of a series of flattened membrane-bound sacs called cisternae.
 
• The Golgi apparatus is critical for processing lysosomal enzymes and ensuring they are delivered to lysosomes.
 
 
 
• **Lysosomes**
 
 
• Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles containing hydrolytic enzymes that break down waste materials and cellular debris.
 
• They play a key role in intracellular digestion and recycling of cellular components.
 
• Lysosomes maintain an acidic environment optimal for enzyme activity.
 
 
 
• **Ribosomes**
 
 
• Ribosomes are molecular machines responsible for protein synthesis in the cell.
 
• They can be found free in the cytoplasm or attached to the rough ER.
 
• Ribosomes translate mRNA into polypeptide chains, which are then folded into functional proteins.

questions.question: __________ was well known for creating fusion art by adapting European theatrical techniques to Indian classical dance combined with Indian folk and tribal dance.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uday Shankar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Uday Shankar was a pioneering Indian dancer and choreographer who is credited with creating a new fusion style of dance.
 
• He combined European theatrical techniques with traditional Indian classical dance forms, as well as Indian folk and tribal dance.
 
• Uday Shankar's innovative approach helped to modernize Indian dance and brought it to an international audience.
 
• He founded the Uday Shankar India Culture Centre in Almora in 1938 to train dancers in his unique style.
 
• His influence extended to the realms of film and music, where he collaborated with various artists to promote Indian culture globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fusion Dance**

 
 
• A dance style that blends elements from different genres and traditions to create a new, hybrid form.
 
• It often involves the integration of classical, folk, and contemporary dance techniques.
 
 
 
• **Classical Dance in India**
 
 
• India has several classical dance forms, such as Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Odissi, and Kathakali.
 
• These dances are characterized by their complex movements, expressions, and storytelling through dance.
 
 
 
• **Indian Folk Dance**
 
 
• Folk dances in India are diverse and reflect the cultural traditions of various regions.
 
• They are often performed during festivals, weddings, and other community celebrations.
 
 
 
• **European Theatrical Techniques**
 
 
• These techniques include elements of staging, lighting, and choreography that are commonly used in Western theater productions.
 
• Incorporating these techniques can enhance the visual and dramatic appeal of dance performances.

questions.question: What is the primary gas responsible for the leavening effect in bread when yeast ferments sugars?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon dioxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Carbon dioxide (CO₂) is the primary gas responsible for the leavening effect in bread when yeast ferments sugars.
 
• Yeast, a microorganism, consumes the sugars present in the dough and produces carbon dioxide and alcohol as by-products.
 
• The carbon dioxide gas gets trapped within the dough, causing it to expand and rise, resulting in the soft and airy texture of bread.
 
• Besides carbon dioxide, the fermentation process also produces ethanol, but this evaporates during baking.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Yeast Fermentation:**

 
 
• Yeast fermentation is a metabolic process that converts sugar into acids, gases, or alcohol.
 
• Saccharomyces cerevisiae is the most commonly used yeast in bread making.
 
 
 
• **Leavening Agents:**
 
 
• Leavening agents are substances used in dough and batter to produce a foaming action, which lightens and softens the finished product.
 
• Besides yeast, other leavening agents include baking soda (sodium bicarbonate) and baking powder.
 
 
 
• **Proofing:**
 
 
• Proofing is the process of allowing dough to rise before baking.
 
• During proofing, yeast ferments the dough, producing carbon dioxide and causing the dough to expand.
 
 
 
• **Gluten:**
 
 
• Gluten is a protein found in wheat, barley, and rye that gives dough its elasticity.
 
• It helps trap carbon dioxide produced by yeast, aiding in the rising process.

questions.question: Who was the famous Venetian traveller of the 13th century who visited Kerala?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Marco Polo**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Marco Polo** was a Venetian merchant and explorer who traveled extensively in the 13th century.
 
• He is renowned for his travels through Asia, documented in his book **"The Travels of Marco Polo"**, which provides a detailed account of his journeys.
 
• Marco Polo visited several regions including China, India, and Persia, and his travels brought him to the southern part of India, including Kerala.
 
• His observations and writings offered Europeans a glimpse into the cultures and practices of the East during the medieval period.
 
• Marco Polo's journey to Kerala is notable for his detailed descriptions of the local economy, culture, and the spice trade that the region was famous for.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nicolo Conti**

 
 
• Nicolo Conti was an Italian merchant and explorer from Venice who traveled to India in the 15th century.
 
• His travel accounts provide valuable insights into the social and economic conditions of India during that time.
 
• He is known for his visit to the Vijayanagara Empire in South India.
 
 
 
• **Abdur Razzaq**
 
 
• Abdur Razzaq was a Persian scholar and diplomat who visited India in the 15th century.
 
• He served as an ambassador to the court of the Vijayanagara Empire.
 
• His writings offer a detailed account of the political and cultural landscape of medieval India.
 
 
 
• **Barthema**
 
 
• Ludovico di Varthema, also known as Barthema, was an Italian traveler and writer.
 
• He visited India in the early 16th century.
 
• His travel narratives provide insights into the trade and customs of the regions he visited, including Kerala.
 
 
 
• **Spice Trade in Kerala**
 
 
• Kerala, located on the southwestern coast of India, was historically known for its spice trade, particularly in pepper, cardamom, and cinnamon.
 
• The region attracted traders from various parts of the world, including Europe, the Middle East, and China.
 
• Ancient ports like Muziris (modern-day Kodungallur) played a crucial role in facilitating trade between Kerala and other civilizations.

questions.question: What is Cash Reserve Ratio?

options.text: Percentage of deposits that a central bank must keep as cash reserves with the bank
Percentage of deposits that a central bank must keep as cash reserves with the government
Percentage of deposits that a bank must keep as cash reserves with any bank
Percentage of deposits that a bank must keep as cash reserves with the central bank

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Percentage of deposits that a bank must keep as cash reserves with the central bank**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is a crucial monetary policy tool used by central banks to control liquidity and inflation.
 
• Banks are mandated to keep a certain percentage of their deposits as cash reserves with the central bank.
 
• CRR ensures that banks do not run out of cash to meet the withdrawal demands of their customers.
 
• Higher CRR reduces the money available for banks to lend, thus controlling inflation, while a lower CRR increases the lending capacity of banks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)**

 
 
• Banks are required to maintain a certain percentage of their net demand and time liabilities (NDTL) in the form of liquid assets like cash, gold, or government securities.
 
• SLR is used by central banks to regulate the credit growth in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Monetary Policy**
 
 
• Monetary policy refers to the actions undertaken by a nation's central bank to control money supply and achieve macroeconomic goals such as controlling inflation, consumption, growth, and liquidity.
 
• Central banks use tools like CRR, SLR, repo rate, and reverse repo rate to implement monetary policy.
 
 
 
• **Repo Rate**
 
 
• The rate at which the central bank of a country lends money to commercial banks in the event of any shortfall of funds.
 
• It is used by monetary authorities to control inflation.
 
 
 
• **Reverse Repo Rate**
 
 
• The rate at which the central bank borrows money from commercial banks within the country.
 
• It is a monetary policy instrument which can be used to control the money supply in the country.

questions.question: Sarhul is an agricultural festival of tribals, which is primarily celebrated in the Indian state of _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jharkhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sarhul is an important festival for tribal communities, particularly the Munda, Oraon, and Ho tribes, primarily celebrated in Jharkhand.
 
• The festival marks the beginning of the New Year and the advent of the spring season.
 
• It involves worshipping trees and nature, signifying the harmony between humans and nature.
 
• Traditional rituals include the offering of flowers and leaves to the village deity, and the celebration involves singing, dancing, and feasting.
 
• Sarhul is observed on the third day of the moon or the fortnight of Chaitra, as per the Hindu calendar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chhau Dance**

 
 
• Chhau Dance is a traditional tribal dance form associated with the state of Jharkhand.
 
• It incorporates martial arts, mock combat, and folklore, often performed during festivals like Sarhul.
 
• The dance is known for its vigorous movements and elaborate masks.
 
• It is recognized as an intangible cultural heritage by UNESCO.
 
 
 
• **Santhal Tribe**
 
 
• The Santhal tribe is one of the largest tribal communities in Jharkhand.
 
• They are known for their rich cultural heritage, including music, dance, and traditional crafts.
 
• Their primary occupation is agriculture and they celebrate several nature-centric festivals.
 
• The Santhal rebellion of 1855-56 is a significant event in Indian history, showcasing their fight against British colonial rule.
 
 
 
• **Jharkhand Cuisine**
 
 
• The cuisine of Jharkhand is known for its simplicity and use of local ingredients.
 
• Popular dishes include Dhuska, Litti Chokha, and Rugra.
 
• Traditional meals often include rice, lentils, vegetables, and a variety of pickles.
 
• Festivals and celebrations feature special dishes prepared with seasonal and local produce.
 
 
 
• **Geography of Jharkhand**
 
 
• Jharkhand is located in eastern India, sharing borders with Bihar, West Bengal, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The state is known for its rich mineral resources, including coal, iron ore, copper, and mica.
 
• It has a diverse landscape with forests, hills, and rivers, contributing to its significant biodiversity.
 
• The state capital is Ranchi, which is a major center for education and industry.

questions.question: According to Census 2011, what is the sex ratio of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**943**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to Census 2011, the sex ratio of India is **943 females per 1000 males**.
 
• The sex ratio is a key demographic indicator that reflects the number of females per 1000 males in a population.
 
• The sex ratio in India has shown an improvement from 933 in Census 2001 to 943 in Census 2011.
 
• The state of Kerala has the highest sex ratio of 1084, while Haryana has the lowest sex ratio of 879 as per Census 2011.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sex Ratio**

 
 
• The sex ratio is a critical social indicator to measure the extent of gender equality in a society.
 
• It is influenced by various factors including birth rates, death rates, and migration patterns.
 
 
 
• **Child Sex Ratio**
 
 
• The child sex ratio (0-6 years) in Census 2011 is 919 females per 1000 males.
 
• This ratio is a significant indicator as it reflects the gender equality at birth and early childhood.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Balanced Sex Ratio**
 
 
• A balanced sex ratio is crucial for the stability of a society and ensures equal opportunities for both genders.
 
• An imbalanced sex ratio can lead to various social issues such as skewed marriage patterns, increased gender-based violence, and societal instability.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives**
 
 
• The Indian government has launched various initiatives like Beti Bachao Beti Padhao to improve the sex ratio.
 
• These programs aim to address the root causes of gender inequality and promote the value of girl children in society.

questions.question: Kalamandalam Krishnan Nair was a notable figure in which of the following classical dance forms of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathakali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kalamandalam Krishnan Nair** was a prominent Kathakali artist from Kerala, India.
 
• He was renowned for his **versatility and exceptional skill** in portraying a wide range of characters in Kathakali performances.
 
• Kalamandalam Krishnan Nair played a pivotal role in **reviving and popularizing Kathakali** in the modern era.
 
• He was honored with numerous awards, including the **Padma Shri** and the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award**.
 
• He was a dedicated teacher at Kerala Kalamandalam, contributing significantly to the training of the next generation of Kathakali artists.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathakali**

 
 
• Kathakali is a classical dance-drama form that originated in Kerala, India.
 
• It is known for its elaborate costumes, intricate makeup, detailed gestures, and well-defined body movements.
 
• Kathakali performances are based on themes from Hindu epics like the Ramayana and Mahabharata.
 
• The dance form combines elements of dance, drama, music, and ritual.
 
• Musicians and vocalists play a crucial role in Kathakali, providing the rhythmic and narrative support for the performance.
 
 
 
• **Bharatanatyam**
 
 
• Originating from Tamil Nadu, Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms in India.
 
• It is characterized by its fixed upper torso, bent legs, and intricate footwork combined with expressive hand gestures.
 
• Bharatanatyam is traditionally performed by women and is known for its grace, purity, tenderness, and sculpturesque poses.
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi**
 
 
• Kuchipudi is a classical Indian dance form from Andhra Pradesh.
 
• It involves fast rhythmic footwork, dramatic characterization, and expressive eye movements.
 
• Kuchipudi performances often narrate stories from Hindu epics and mythology.
 
 
 
• **Mohiniyattam**
 
 
• Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form from Kerala, traditionally performed by women.
 
• It is known for its graceful and sensuous movements, resembling the dance of the celestial enchantress Mohini.
 
• Mohiniyattam includes elements of both Bharatanatyam and Kathakali in its performance style.

questions.question: Who was the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India for the 2011 Indian Census?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr. C Chandramouli**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dr. C Chandramouli served as the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India during the 2011 Census.
 
• The 2011 Census was the 15th National Census of India since 1872.
 
• Dr. C Chandramouli is an Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer from the Tamil Nadu cadre of the 1985 batch.
 
• The 2011 Census involved a massive exercise of data collection, covering over 1.2 billion people.
 
• The Census was conducted in two phases: the house-listing and housing census phase and the population enumeration phase.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India**

 
 
• The office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India falls under the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.
 
• This office is responsible for conducting and managing the demographic surveys, including the Census and the Civil Registration System (CRS).
 
• The Census of India is one of the largest administrative exercises conducted in the world.
 
• The Census data is crucial for planning and policy-making at various levels of government.
 
 
 
• **Indian Census**
 
 
• The first synchronous census was conducted in India in 1881.
 
• The Indian Census is conducted once every 10 years.
 
• The data collected includes demographic, socio-economic, and cultural information.
 
• The Census helps in determining the population size, growth rate, density, sex ratio, literacy rate, and other vital statistics.
 
 
 
• **2011 Indian Census Highlights**
 
 
• India's population as per the 2011 Census was 1.21 billion.
 
• The literacy rate in 2011 was 74.04%, a significant increase from the previous census.
 
• The sex ratio was 943 females per 1000 males.
 
• The state of Uttar Pradesh had the highest population, while Sikkim had the least.
 
 
 
• **Use of Technology in Census**
 
 
• The 2011 Census saw the use of technology for data collection and processing.
 
• Handheld devices were used for data entry in some areas to improve accuracy and efficiency.
 
• GIS (Geographic Information Systems) was utilized to map data geographically.
 
• Technology played a significant role in ensuring a more streamlined and error-free census process.

questions.question: Helium gas can be converted to the liquid form by the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**London forces of attraction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Helium gas can be liquefied due to the presence of weak intermolecular forces known as **London dispersion forces**.
 
• These forces arise from the momentary distribution of electrons in an atom, leading to a temporary dipole.
 
• London forces are the only intermolecular forces that act between helium atoms, which are non-polar.
 
• Despite being weak, these forces are sufficient to hold helium atoms together in the liquid state at very low temperatures.
 
• **Heike Kamerlingh Onnes** was the first to liquefy helium in 1908 by cooling it to below its boiling point of 4.2 K.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Intermolecular Forces**

 
 
• These are forces of attraction or repulsion between neighboring particles (atoms, molecules, or ions).
 
• Types include London dispersion forces, dipole-dipole interactions, and hydrogen bonding.
 
• London dispersion forces are the weakest, while hydrogen bonds are the strongest among them.
 
 
 
• **Helium**
 
 
• Helium is a noble gas with the atomic number 2 and is the second lightest and second most abundant element in the observable universe.
 
• It is colorless, odorless, tasteless, non-toxic, and inert, making it extremely stable.
 
 
 
• **Liquefaction of Gases**
 
 
• This process involves cooling a gas to a temperature below its critical point, where it can condense into a liquid.
 
• It is used in various industrial processes, including the production of liquefied natural gas (LNG).
 
 
 
• **Critical Temperature**
 
 
• The highest temperature at which a substance can exist as a liquid is called its critical temperature.
 
• For helium, this temperature is extremely low, making its liquefaction a significant scientific achievement.

questions.question: The sister of Harshavardhana Rajyashri was married to__________, the king of Maukhari dynasty of Kanyakubja.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Grahavarman**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Rajyashri, the sister of Harshavardhana, was married to Grahavarman.
 
• Grahavarman was the king of the Maukhari dynasty, which ruled over Kanyakubja (modern-day Kannauj).
 
• The Maukhari dynasty played a significant role in the political landscape of northern India during the early medieval period.
 
• The marriage alliance between Rajyashri and Grahavarman helped strengthen the political ties between the Vardhana dynasty and the Maukhari dynasty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Harshavardhana**

 
 
• Harshavardhana, also known as Harsha, was a prominent Indian emperor who ruled North India from 606 to 647 CE.
 
• He belonged to the Vardhana dynasty and was known for his efforts to establish a strong and unified empire in northern India.
 
• Harsha was a patron of arts and culture, and his court was adorned with scholars like Banabhatta and Xuanzang.
 
• His reign marked a period of prosperity and cultural flourishing in North India.
 
 
 
• **Maukhari Dynasty**
 
 
• The Maukhari dynasty was an influential ruling dynasty in North India during the 6th and 7th centuries CE.
 
• They initially served as vassals of the Gupta Empire before establishing their independent rule.
 
• The Maukhari rulers were known for their administrative efficiency and military prowess.
 
• Their capital was Kanyakubja (Kannauj), which became a significant center of power in North India.
 
 
 
• **Kanyakubja (Kannauj)**
 
 
• Kanyakubja, also known as Kannauj, is an ancient city located in the present-day Indian state of Uttar Pradesh.
 
• It has been a prominent political, cultural, and commercial center since ancient times.
 
• Kannauj was known for its rich cultural heritage and was a major center of learning and arts.
 
• Throughout history, Kannauj has been a coveted seat of power for various dynasties, including the Maukhari and the Vardhana dynasties.
 
 
 
• **Political Alliances in Ancient India**
 
 
• Marriage alliances were a common strategy for establishing political ties and securing peace between different dynasties.
 
• Such alliances helped in strengthening mutual trust and cooperation between ruling families.
 
• They played a crucial role in the consolidation of power and expansion of empires in ancient India.
 
• These alliances also facilitated cultural exchange and integration between different regions.

questions.question: Pandit Arvind Thatte belongs to which of the following gharanas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mewati gharana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pandit Arvind Thatte is a renowned harmonium player associated with the **Mewati gharana**.
 
• The Mewati gharana was founded by Ustad Ghagge Nazir Khan in the late 19th century.
 
• This gharana is known for its emphasis on the emotional expression and devotional elements of Hindustani classical music.
 
• Pandit Arvind Thatte has accompanied many legendary musicians, including Pandit Jasraj, who is also a prominent figure in the Mewati gharana.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mewati gharana**

 
 
• It emphasizes clarity in the rendition of ragas, intricate taans (rapid melodic passages), and a blend of khayal and devotional music.
 
• The gharana has produced several notable musicians, including Pandit Jasraj, Pandit Sanjeev Abhyankar, and Pandita Tripti Mukherjee.
 
• Mewati gharana performances often incorporate elements from other gharanas, making their style versatile and unique.
 
 
 
• **Harmonium**
 
 
• The harmonium is a keyboard instrument that produces sound when air flows over free metal reeds.
 
• It is widely used in Indian classical music, devotional music, and various folk traditions.
 
• The instrument is played with one hand operating the bellows and the other pressing the keys.
 
 
 
• **Pandit Jasraj**
 
 
• Pandit Jasraj was a legendary Indian classical vocalist belonging to the Mewati gharana.
 
• He was known for his soulful renditions, extensive repertoire, and for popularizing the Mewati gharana globally.
 
• Pandit Jasraj received numerous awards, including the Padma Vibhushan, India's second-highest civilian honor.

questions.question: In the inaugural year of the Nehru Cup event for football in 1982, which team emerged as the winner of the first edition?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uruguay**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Uruguay won the inaugural Nehru Cup in 1982, held in India.
 
• The Nehru Cup was initiated to promote international football in India.
 
• The tournament attracted several international teams, enhancing its prestige.
 
• Uruguay's victory in the first edition set a high standard for the competition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nehru Cup**

 
 
• The Nehru Cup is an international football tournament organized by the All India Football Federation (AIFF).
 
• It was named after Jawaharlal Nehru, the first Prime Minister of India.
 
• The tournament has been held intermittently since its inception in 1982.
 
• The format typically includes national teams from various countries, contributing to its competitive nature.
 
 
 
• **Uruguay National Football Team**
 
 
• Uruguay is known for its strong footballing tradition and success on the international stage.
 
• The team has won the FIFA World Cup twice, in 1930 and 1950.

• The AIFF is the governing body for football in India, responsible for organizing national competitions and managing the national team.

• The AIFF aims to develop and promote football at all levels in India.
 
• It organizes several tournaments, including the I-League and Indian Super League (ISL).

questions.question: Who among the following is the ex-officio Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha as on 10 October 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jagdeep Dhankar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As of 10 October 2023, Jagdeep Dhankar is the ex-officio Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha.
 
• He holds the position by virtue of being the Vice President of India.
 
• Jagdeep Dhankar assumed office as the Vice President of India on 11 August 2022.
 
• The Vice President of India automatically becomes the Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha upon taking office.
 
• The Rajya Sabha, also known as the Council of States, is the upper house of India's bicameral Parliament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Role of the Vice President**

 
 
• The Vice President is the second-highest constitutional office in India, after the President.
 
• The Vice President's primary duty is to act as the Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha.
 
• In the event of the President's death, resignation, or removal, the Vice President may act as the President until a new President is elected.
 
 
 
• **Rajya Sabha (Council of States)**
 
 
• The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body and is not subject to dissolution, unlike the Lok Sabha.
 
• Members of the Rajya Sabha are elected by the elected members of State Legislative Assemblies and by the members of the Electoral college for Union Territories.
 
• One-third of the members of the Rajya Sabha retire every two years.
 
 
 
• **Functions of the Rajya Sabha Chairperson**
 
 
• The Chairperson presides over the sessions of the Rajya Sabha.
 
• He/she ensures the orderly conduct of business and adherence to parliamentary procedures and rules.
 
• The Chairperson has the authority to discipline members for unruly behavior and can suspend them if necessary.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**
 
 
• The position of Vice President and Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha was established by the Constitution of India, which came into effect on 26 January 1950.
 
• Dr. S. Radhakrishnan was the first Vice President of India and the first Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha.
